[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The self-managed worker Auto Scaling group can begin launching nodes before the `aws-auth` ConfigMap is installed. The module explicitly gates managed node groups on this ConfigMap to avoid node registration races; this ASG needs the same ordering.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
The Auto Scaling group can launch worker instances before :resource.kubernetes_config_map.aws_auth maps their IAM role, creating a race in which the nodes cannot authenticate to the cluster.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
Worker instances can launch before the aws-auth ConfigMap maps their IAM roles, so `:resource.aws_autoscaling_group.workers` should wait for `:resource.kubernetes_config_map.aws_auth` to avoid nodes attempting to join before authentication is configured.

----------------------------------------

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
`aws_autoscaling_group.workers` instances boot and immediately try to register with the cluster, authenticating with the worker IAM role, which must already be mapped in the `aws-auth` ConfigMap (`kubernetes_config_map.aws_auth`). The ASG only depends on the cluster, launch configuration and `random_pet.workers`, so instances can launch before the ConfigMap maps their role and fail to join the cluster. This operational ordering is not expressed anywhere; it needs an explicit `depends_on = [kubernetes_config_map.aws_auth]`.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
`resource.aws_autoscaling_group.workers` launches self-managed EKS worker instances that authenticate to the cluster via the `aws-auth` ConfigMap (their role ARN is templated into `local.configmap_roles`), but nothing orders the ASG after `kubernetes_config_map.aws_auth`: the ASG's expressions only reference the cluster name, launch configuration and random_pet. The module authors added exactly this ordering to the managed node groups via `ng_depends_on` (which includes `kubernetes_config_map.aws_auth`) to avoid nodes being created before they can authenticate; the self-managed ASG has the same race and needs an explicit `depends_on` (or an equivalent reference) on the ConfigMap.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The self-managed worker Auto Scaling group can launch instances before the worker-node IAM policy is attached, so instances may start without the permissions needed to join and operate in the cluster. Gate the ASG on this attachment, as the module does for managed node groups.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
The Auto Scaling group launches worker instances but does not wait for :resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.workers_AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy; instances can start before their IAM role has the worker-node permissions required to join the cluster.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The Auto Scaling group may launch workers before the required EKS worker-node policy is attached; `:resource.aws_autoscaling_group.workers` should depend on `:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.workers_AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy` so instances have the permissions needed to register and operate.

----------------------------------------

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
aws_autoscaling_group.workers launches EKS worker instances as soon as the ASG is created, but nothing orders it after the AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy attachment on the worker IAM role. Instances launched before the policy is attached will fail to authenticate/join the cluster (and slow or break cluster formation). The node_groups submodule guards this exact race via ng_depends_on; the legacy ASG path does not.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
The EKS AMI bootstrap script authenticates with the node IAM role and calls aws eks describe-cluster, which requires the AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy attachment (and IAM changes propagate with delay). The ASG only transitively depends on the IAM role via the launch configuration's instance profile, not on the policy attachments, so instances can boot before the policy is attached and bootstrap then fails so the node never joins. The node_groups module waits for these attachments via ng_depends_on; the ASG does not. No implicit reference or data fix exists; a bare depends_on is needed.

The self-managed worker Auto Scaling group can launch instances before the EKS CNI policy is attached, creating a race where nodes start without the required CNI permissions. Gate the ASG on this attachment, as the module does for managed node groups.

----------------------------------------

The Auto Scaling group launches worker instances but does not wait for :resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.workers_AmazonEKS_CNI_Policy; instances can start before the worker role's CNI permissions are attached.

----------------------------------------

The Auto Scaling group may launch workers before the CNI policy is attached; `:resource.aws_autoscaling_group.workers` should depend on `:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.workers_AmazonEKS_CNI_Policy` so the worker role has its configured networking permissions before instances start.
